content: Run GitHub Script Overview This basic template demonstrates how to run a GitHub script (locally) using a personal access token for authentication. Prerequisites - Node.js and npm installed. - A personal access token with the necessary permissions for your GitHub repository. Optional dependencies - gh (GitHub CLI) installed and authenticated with your user. This is optional but recommended for easier token management. NPM Dependencies - @actions/github: Official GitHub Actions toolkit for interacting with the GitHub API. - @actions/core: Official GitHub Actions toolkit for core functionalities like setting outputs and handling errors. - @octokit/rest: Official GitHub REST API client for JavaScript. Setup 1. Clone the repository containing the GitHub script. 1. Navigate to the repository directory. 1. Install the necessary dependencies using npm: Usage The GITHUB TOKEN environment variable is used for authentication. If you have a personal access token, or do not wish to use the GitHub CLI (gh), you can set it directly in the environment variable before running the script. Using main.sh (recommended) The main.sh script checks for gh (GitHub CLI) and uses it to retrieve the personal access token if GITHUB TOKEN is not set. The main.sh script is a wrapper that handles loading environment variables and running the GitHub script.
